## Part 1.1 : Creative Ideation

1. This course should have more programming exercises because it will give students more practice with programming.
2. This course should have memory-diagram drawings for homework to encourage students to get more comfortable at drawing them.
3. This course should have optional feedback at the end of homeworks to let instructors know if there is a concept/function that a large amount of people struggle with.
4. This course should add class time to review code with another student to encourage collaboration with other students and allow them to learn from each others mistakes.
5. This course should have more quizzes but shorter in length so that students don't have to study or remember as much material, making students feel less stressed and inspires students to study more consistently.

## Part 1.2: Identifying Missing Data

1. Idea without sufficient data to analyze:
Idea #4: Review code with another student
2. Suggestion for how to collect data to support this idea in the future: 
There could be two questions where the first one asks for the amount of times you review code with another classmate (on a scale 0-10 where 0 means never and 10 means all of the time). Then the follow-up question could ask if those discussions were helpful or not (0 being not helpful at all and 10 being very helpful).

## Part 1.3: Choosing Your Analysis

1. Idea to analyze with available data:
Idea #1: More programming exercises
2. This idea is more valuable than the others brainstormed because: 
Being able to write code is the most valuble skill that comes from this class. Although the other ideas are important, being able to accurately and confidently write code is the most important.

## Part 1.5: Conclusion

In conclusion the data supports the idea that there should be more programming exercises. Students who found programming exercises to be the most effective for them (rated a 7) had an average understanding score of 4.86 compared to just 2.50 for those who rated the programming exercises a 2. This was the trend for all ratings where the higher the programming exercise effectiveness, the higher the understanding. The prior experience was also analyzed to see if those with more experience didn't find the exercises useful. However, they followed the same trend where the more they thought the exercises were helpful, the higher the understanding. This shows that the programming exercises are very useful to help students understand programming better (regardless of experience), supporting the argument that there should be more programming exercises. The negative trade-offs would be that the instructor of the course would have to change the structure of the course to make more exercises. The other negative trade-off would be more course-work for the students and more exercises that get graded by the instructors/TAs. This could add extra stress for both parties, however in the end make the students more confident and advanced with programming.
